text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a reconnect spike right after yesterday's console canary (20%). It looks correlated with tenant throttles: clients try to resume, get rejected, then hammer reconnects.
kevin: Confirming. Dashboard shows a 3x reconnect rate for t-1234 between 11:02-11:07. Sample logs:
```
[11:03:12] conn=abc123 tenant=t-1234 -> 429 quota exceeded
[11:03:12] conn=abc123 client reconnect attempt (resume_token=rt-987)
[11:03:12] conn=abc123 -> 204 no content (socket closed)
```
sara: Is the client getting a resume accepted then later receiving a 429 on the resumed request, or are we rejecting resume attempts outright? That changes the dedupe/billing model.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout: console/service-config v2.14 -> 20% (2026-03-10T11:00Z)
kevin: This looks like resume is accepted at the proxy but the upstream quota check later fails when request hits runtime. So client thinks resume succeeded, then runtime denies and we end up with an ambiguous state.
paul: If resume acceptance isn't transactional with quota allocation, we can end up double-charging or replay. We should avoid accepting resume unless we can reserve capacity or mark it for soft-fail.
jen: Double-charge is real — we saw a similar edge in /dedicated where retried chunks counted twice. Need explicit idempotency markers or a resume-accept -> commit flow.
maria: Proposal: introduce a short "grace" window on resume acceptance. Option A: proxy returns a control event telling client to backoff (soft throttle) for X seconds instead of outright closing. Option B: proxy accepts resume but marks session as "provisional" and runtime must confirm within N ms or we reject and return a control event.
sara: Also consider protocol differences: SSE supports the `retry:` field; WS doesn't. We need a protocol-agnostic control message. Maybe a JSON event with type=control/backoff.
kevin: Quick prototype header idea: `X-Reconnect-After: 3000` on 429-like responses. But proxies strip non-standard headers sometimes.
paul: Agree with sara — use an in-stream control event. For SSE:
```
event: control
data: {"type":"backoff","backoff_ms":3000,"reason":"tenant_quota"}

```
For WS, send `{ "event":"control", "type":"backoff", "backoff_ms":3000 }` as a JSON frame.
jen: Careful: some clients auto-retry on network close and ignore control events. We need to document client-side behavior for SDKs and maybe enforce server-side token expiry to avoid fast hammering.
maria: Telemetry: add tags `reconnect_reason` (quota|network|proxy), `resume_outcome` (accepted|provisional|rejected), and a boolean `control_event_sent`. Sample 10% of traces at full debug; aggregate counts for 100%.
kevin: Also add a `soft_throttle` flag so console can show when a tenant is being gently pushed to backoff vs hard-blocked. Makes rolling back easier UX-wise.
sara: Another practical gotcha: CDN/proxy may buffer or coalesce SSE events into one TCP packet and some clients parse incorrectly. We'll add an extra `\n` separator and unique `id` per control event to be safe.
paul: From infra side: we should implement server-side soft quota which doesn't consume billing credits during grace. Only if client actually sends tokens/requests after grace do we bill. That prevents accidental double-billing if resume ultimately rejected.
jen: QA checklist: repro with simple JS SSE client + WS client, simulate runtime quota delay, validate that control event causes SDK backoff and that no duplicate billing occurs.
ops-bot: Alert: tenant t-1234 quota spike threshold breached 3x (11:04) — investigating.
maria: OK — action items:
- kevin: spike dashboard + add `reconnect_reason` metrics (PR)
- sara: design control event schema + SSE/WS examples (doc)
- paul: implement provisional resume flow on proxy + runtime confirm API (proto)
- jen: update SDKs to respect control events and add idempotency marker handling
- QA: create repro and test cases
Please add PR links here once created. I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow 10:30 to unblock rollout decisions. :spiral_calendar:
